# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 96 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 96 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_096_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9 — The Gate Is Both Old and New

**1** "Lord, explain the mountain covered in the richest green grass where animals grazed and birds came to rest," I asked. **2** "When the peoples of every nation under heaven heard and believed," he said, "they were brought into the name of the Son of God. **3** Receiving the seal — baptism — they were given one heart, one mind, one faith, one love. They also carried the spirits of the virgins with them. That is why the tower appears to be built from a single stone." **4** "And what does the gate mean?" I asked. **5** "Every stone that entered the tower," he said, "had to pass through the gate — and the gate is the Son of God. **6** He is the only way in to the Lord. There is no other path to him than through his Son. **7** Look at that gate — it is ancient, yet entirely new! The grace that comes through it is fresh and alive, and those who enter through it are blessed — they believe and they live." **8** "How can it be both ancient and new?" I asked. **9** "Because the Son of God is older than all creation," he said, "and was present as God's counselor when everything was made. **10** That's why he is ancient. But the gate appeared as something new in these last days — so that everyone who is to be saved can walk through it into God's kingdom. **11** Did you notice how every stone that came through the gate entered the tower — but those that didn't come through it were sent back?" **12** "Yes, Lord," I said. "In exactly the same way," he said, "no one enters God's kingdom without receiving the name of his Son. **13** Think of it this way: if you want to get into a walled city that has only one gate, can you enter any other way than through that gate? **14** Likewise, no one enters God's kingdom except through the name of his Son — his beloved Son. Did you see the great crowd of those who were building the tower?" "Yes, Lord, I saw them."

---

*PNEUMA renders the gate's paradox — ancient/new — and the city-gate analogy with accessible directness, emphasizing the universal scope of the gospel invitation.*
